newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani bourse to start on-line trading Dec 30.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani bourse to start on-line trading Dec 30.

text.p: The Lahore Stock Exchange (LSE) will become Pakistan's first bourse to switch over to modern on-line trading from December 30, a Corporate Law Authority (CLA) official said.

"The CLA has approved trading regulations for the Lahore stock market to replace the old manual trading, which will eliminate the chances of any manipulation," CLA member Jamil Ahmed Bhutto told Reuters.

He said the computerised on-line trading would be done in all scrips barring the shares of telecom utility Pakistan Telecommunicationc Company Ltd (PTCL). "PTCL is a big scrip, but we hope to start its on-line trading in another month or so."
Bhutto said the system installed at the Lahore bourse was the most modern and sophisticated in Pakistan and would ensure openness, credibility and transparency of the deals.
Investors at Pakistan's three bourses, including the main Karachi Stock Exchange, have often complained of manipulation in deals and delays in carrying out their orders.
"We chose the LSE for on-line trading because it is relatively a new bourse where there is less resistance to change and modernisation."
The Karachi bourse has been doing computerised trading in the evening on a trial basis for the last six months.
He said the new system at Lahore had been tested and tried for almost two years before the CLA gave a go-ahead for the switchover.
